Registered residential sales reached 13,707 units in the last four weeks, totaling AED 39.49bn. This represents a 24.1% increase in volume and a 23.1% rise in value compared to the previous four weeks. Mortgage registrations are tracked separately and totaled 5,556 during the same period. The data reflects a clear acceleration in transaction activity across the market.

The median residential price per square foot rose to AED 1,727, marking a 3.4% increase from the prior period. Off-plan transactions accounted for 56.7% of all sales. Among top performing areas, Dubai South led with 2,736 sales over twelve weeks, while Dubai Creek Harbour showed the strongest price momentum at AED 2,528 per square foot.

Rental activity remained robust with 107,552 Ejari contracts registered. Renewals comprised 51.9% of these contracts, and the median residential rent stood at AED 68,000 annually. International City Phase 1 recorded the highest estimated gross yield at 8.6% for flats, followed by Zaabeel First at 7.9%. These yields reflect current market conditions for specific property types within those communities.

Investors should monitor Al Yufrah 1, which saw a 33.0% price increase over twelve weeks, alongside cooling in Saih Shuaib 1 at minus 29.6%. The anomaly detector flagged 961 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35% away from comparable medians. Figures are based on registered DLD data and medians, with benchmarks filtering out bulk deals and outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
